title: Dowst humdrum-vs-bizarre narration experiment brief
purpose: Operationalize Dowst's chapter VII claim that humdrum stories call for matter-of-fact succession of details (no highlights) while bizarre stories require either (a) familiar anchoring or (b) vivid/forceful rendering. Provides two matched story seeds, writing instructions for three variants, and a blind-reader discrimination task. Tests whether the prescribed surface differences produce a detectable perceptual difference. Source: art_01M6Q7NRMXHF7YV3PC2WD994D4 r1.
attribution: Dowst, Robert Saunders. The Technique of Fiction Writing. Project Gutenberg eBook 32092. Chapter VII claims restated from art_01M6Q7NRMXHF7YV3PC2WD994D4 r1 (documented, not tested).
